feedback.problem:
An engineer measures the amount of fuel $F$, in liters, remaining in a generator. The following table shows the rate at which fuel is being consumed.

| **$t\,\text{(hours)}$** | $2$ | $4$ | $6$ | $8$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ${F}^{′}(t)\,\text{(liters/hour)}$ | $-3.1$ | $-3.5$ | $-4.0$ | $-4.4$ |

At $t=4,$ the generator contained $62$ liters of fuel. Use the tangent line approximation of $F$ at time $t=4$ to estimate the amount of fuel remaining at $t=4.6.$  Do not round the answer.

The amount of fuel remaining at $t=4.6$ hours is estimated to be
{{field-1}}
liters.
feedback.worked_solution:
The tangent line approximation of $F(t)$ at the point $a=4$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}L(t) & =F(a)+{F}^{′}(a)(t-a) \\  & =F(4)+{F}^{′}(4)(t-4) \\  & =62-3.5(t-4).\end{aligned}
$$

We can approximate $F(4.6)$ by evaluating the tangent line approximation at $t=4.6.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}F(4.6) & ≈L(4.6) \\  & =62-3.5(4.6-4) \\  & =62-3.5(0.6) \\  & =62-2.1 \\  & =59.9.\end{aligned}
$$

The amount of fuel remaining at $t=4.6$ hours is estimated to be $59.9$ liters.
